DEFAULT_WINDOW is 2020-2025 (about 6 years; 2026 partial and excluded by default). Nine study sectors are listed in sgs_config.R.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's simulations are balanced clusters of 5 with Gaussian-copula correlation, not two-way designs. The direction (SEs too small below G = 10) transfers qualitatively; the size of the bias for the study's sector x year design is not measured. The analyst's 9 x 4 design is not traced in code.
bearings.verifier_note: Code window is 2020-2025, not 2020-2026. Exp IV says 'in most cases', not all. The year-dimension caution comes from Sec 5.2, not Exp IV; the bearing mixes the two under one label.

bearings.paper_claim: Exp IV: for small G the coverage order is HC3 best, then HC2, HC1, HC0. The authors say their results are not consistent with HC3 being overly aggressive, though HC3 slightly over-corrects at G = 10 for binomial. The clustered bootstrap (R = 250) is somewhat better than HC0 and HC1 at small G. Pustejovsky and Tipton (2018) is cited as recommending HC2 with Satterthwaite t.
bearings.system_side: sgs_estimate.R: WCR bootstrap-t with Webb six-point weights, clusters = sectors, CR1 factor G/(G-1)(n-1)/(n-p) in the t statistic (sgs_cr1_factor). A grep of sgs_review.R and sgs_estimate.R finds no CR2 or CR3 error.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's bootstrap is a clustered bootstrap with R = 250; its resampling type is not stated for the simulations, and wild or Webb bootstrap-t is not tested. So the paper cannot rank WCR against CR2 or CR3. The HC3 ranking is for linear and GLM fits with balanced clusters of 5, not two-way designs with about 9 sector clusters.
bearings.verifier_note: 'HC3 is not found overly aggressive' needs the binomial caveat. The paper gives no evidence on WCR versus CR1 t-tests. The no-CR2/CR3 gap is verified by grep. Recommendation is analyst opinion and needs Paul's go under change control.

bearings.paper_claim: Panel PL and PC coverage is poor with short panels (5 observations per cluster) and with exchangeable correlation, where coverage falls as panels lengthen. With decaying AR(1) correlation, coverage rises toward 0.95 as panels lengthen. The paper says some care is needed with panel estimators in short panels or with non-decaying autocorrelation.

bearings.verifier_note: 'Only under decaying AR(1)' and 'fail' overstate the paper, which says coverage deteriorates and needs care. The SEATS-W series has no clusters, so 'supports' is generous; 'context' fits better. Code details verified.

related.why: The paper cites Zeileis 2006b for the object-oriented sandwich framework that vcovCL and vcovPL extend. Verified in the reference list and Sec 3.
The paper cites Zeileis 2004 for the HC and HAC estimators reused in vcovPL and the HC0-HC3 corrections (text ~line 336 and ~line 773). Verified.

summary_issues: Window error: summary says the study has 9 sectors over the 2020-2026 cycles. sgs_config.R DEFAULT_WINDOW is 2020-2025 (about 6 years), 2026 is partial and excluded by default, and the fallback is the latest run of at least 10 years. The 9 study sectors are correct.
The 5-to-9 sector cluster range in the summary is not traced. Config lists 9 study sectors and MIN_SECTORS = 2; the lower bound of 5 needs a per-test count from the study outputs.

Overstatement: summary says panel NW and PCSE fail when panels are short or dependence is exchangeable. The paper says coverage deteriorates and needs care, and that AR(1) improves coverage toward 0.95.

Threshold misattribution: the 50 to 100 cluster threshold for CL-0 comes from Exp IV (Gaussian, binomial, Poisson). Exp III (beta, zero-truncated and zero-inflated Poisson) is run at G = 100 only, so near-0.95 coverage across beta and count models at G = 50 to 100 is not shown.
At G = 10 the paper says standard errors are underestimated in most cases, not all; HC3 is the exception for binomial and Poisson. The summary drops this qualifier.

The summary's judgment that WCR bootstrap-t is the right instinct is analyst opinion, not supported by this paper. vcovBS offers wild, Mammen, Webb and Rademacher types and the paper says Webb may help with few clusters, but these are described, not evaluated.

Missing point: the paper suggests multi0 (basic sandwich in place of the intersection term) when each id-time cell holds one observation. sgs_review.R has no multi0 option. Check whether sector-year cells are singletons before treating Eq 20 without multi0 as the paper's preferred form.
Removed: the code has no sandwich fix = TRUE option, so the claim that a non-positive two-way diagonal is eigen-fixed is wrong. The code only records the non-positive case as a note.
Dropped related link imai-2021-fixed-effects-regression: this paper does not discuss two-way fixed-effects causal inference, and the stated complement is not in the text.

The 1.5 to 2 times SE inflation is from the InstInnovation negative binomial hurdle model (803 company clusters, text ~lines 943-1063). It must be quoted with that window and denominator, not as a general factor.
